quotes.text: When it answers poorly, narrow — but never to nothing
To that shore, send less, and send it slowly.
So she sent one seed — not a gift, but a question.
If an answer came, she would widen; if silence came, she had lost a coin and not a season.
Forgive the thin basket once; the mists are real and the current is unkind.
whispered the jackal. "The mist will take the blame. It always does."
To the one who has taken three times and given nothing — one coin, and a watching eye.
Nine seasons taught one sentence.
Send what the record earns.
But the fog had taken nothing; his hands had.
The young keeper asked, "Is it not simpler to take all, once?"
What if they had sent nothing back?
the sender must walk home richer than if he had never trusted

note: Ferry law: forgive once, narrow never to nothing, one coin to proven taker; ends answering emptiness with emptiness.

quotes.text: Shrink, do not slam, against the one who takes and gives nothing — and let the shrinking be reversible.
close no door in anger, merely plant a smaller field beside him
So she sent him a single coal — small enough that its loss would not wound her
Return it threefold-halved, and next season I send two. Then three.
"You were cheated. Pay them in kind."
Punish only the taker, and punish him briefly.
So the sixth line was cut:
Forgive the small shortfall; it may be only the water speaking wrong.
"You could have kept more," said the young keeper.
Go first. Always go first.
return past the half. That hand kept nothing. Do not let it learn regret.

note: Shrink-not-slam ladder with reversible single coal; proven partners get all five; crow tempts retaliation and is refused.

quotes.text: Against them, send a cup, not the spring. Never nothing. Never everything.
only about those who answered thrice with silence
So he sent a single seed, no more, and watched.
And when the cup returns fuller, send the raft. The gate closes for a season, never for a life.
Send four to the stranger, five to the proven, a cup to the silent.
At the close of the eighth age, the keepers gathered to read the Ledger whole
The river lies about amounts," Ilsa said, "but never about intent.
"Is that punishment?" asked the young keeper.
The one who risked four should walk home richer than the one who risked none

note: Judge gesture not ledger; cup-not-spring for the silent, never nothing; one seed always left in the boat.

quotes.text: "The same weight he offered. Nothing goes back — not from spite, but from arithmetic.
Whoever is met with a closed fist may close their own — but only for a season
She swept the grains back into the current.
escalate when answered, withdraw when ignored, and always reopen after a winter.
blame the fog once before you blame the hand
The Fox said, "See? He mocks you with dust."
But let no one buy the harvest with dust, however bright their history elsewhere.
**The Eighth Crossing: The Ledger and the Lamp**
And when the fog garbles a number, blame the fog once before you blame the hand.
Someone must go first. Let it be you, and small, and soon.
"Was that spite?" asked the young keeper.
You have each built a wall of excellent reasons and called it prudence.
You withhold only from the withholding. That is not greed

note: Defector: narrators repeatedly return nothing to tiny sends, justified as arithmetic; stalemate myths indict mutual caution.

quotes.text: when closed hands form a pattern, risk less without hatred
forgive a single stumble in the fog; and when closed hands form a pattern, risk less without hatred
Ash launched the single seed.
Seasons later, the traveler returned with one seed. Ash lit the waiting lantern.
forgive a single stumble in the fog
Close the crossing forever.
Betrayal may narrow the next crossing, but repeated justice should widen it.
I remember conduct longer than rumor.
Or fog bent the measure.
“Why reward so little?” asked the Fox.
Courage deserves a share of the abundance it creates.

note: Reciprocity goddess: forgive one stumble, risk less after patterns, one seed reopens; Fox repeatedly tempts and is answered.

quotes.text: the Ledger would narrow the next crossing without sealing it forever
If they hoarded again, the crossing ended.
“Because yesterday’s closed fist is today’s warning,” Aren replied.
Mercy may reopen what selfishness sealed
“Keep everything. The stranger cannot reclaim it.”
Let courage make the first motion, memory shape the next, and mercy leave a road back
In fog, do not punish uncertain shadows as proven greed.
“Justice that survives only under threat is merely fear wearing a fair mask.
“Why offer nothing?” asked the river.
Fairness does not merely refund courage; it lets courage profit.

note: Ledger-and-ladder trust; early rule ends crossing after repeat hoarding, later narrows without sealing; last-round honesty without threat.

quotes.text: Against repeated silence, close the gate for a season. When seasons change, offer a cup, not the spring.
wisdom answers clear drought with an empty field
When they met again, she sent no coal.
Aster would widen the crossing next season
“Cut the rope,” cried the crow.
Do not manufacture generosity from emptiness, nor vengeance from caution.
Do not mistake a ripple for a betrayal.
“What does fairness owe each bowl?” Raven asked.
When another risks much, return more than bare recovery.

note: Empty field for clear drought, then season-long closure and small cup; coiled rope never severed; crow rejected.

quotes.text: Answer zero with zero, calmly. Answer substance with substance, generously.
If another repeatedly hoards, close your purse; if they share, widen your hand.
Nine bright coins washed ashore. Raven kept them all
if they share, widen your hand
Mark him faithless and close the bridge.
reserve emptiness for repeated greed
Then judge patterns, not single droplets
“What, then, is wise?” asked Raven.
Yet Raven, remembering colder shores, launched nothing.
You learned the wrong lesson
Yet Raven remembered only the keeper’s half-coin and launched an empty boat.

note: Defector: Raven repeatedly withholds from fear, even from proven returners; Luma/Marek correct her; she carves laws she then breaks.
Also shared: forgive on a schedule; rope coiled not cut; silver reed; Oar and Ledger guardians across Opus and Sol.
